newsitem.title: USA: MCI forms alliance with British, Portuguese firms.
newsitem.headline: MCI forms alliance with British, Portuguese firms.

text.p: MCI Communications said on Monday it has formed a strategic alliance with British Telecommunications plc and Portugal Telecom SA to address growing communications markets in both Portugal and Latin America.
Under the announced pact with MCI and BT, Portugal Telecom would become the exclusive distributor for Concert Communications Services' voice products in Portugal, MCI said in a statement.
It did not comment on a report by Portugal Telecom that MCI and Telefonica International, an arm of Telefonica de Espana, had formed a Pan American joint venture.
Portugal Telecom and MCI would also explore opportunities in Brazil, where Portugal Telecom had an alliance with giant Brazilian telecommunications firm Telebras, MCI said.
The companies would also seek other opportunities in the Latin American communications market, which they valued at $36 billion, MCI added.
As part of the alliance, BT and MCI would take one percent and 0.5 percent equity stakes respectively in Portugal Telecom during its privatisation expected later this year, MCI said.
At that time, a BT executive would be invited to take a seat on the Portugal Telecom board of directors, MCI said.

"We are pleased that Portugal Telecom has selected us to offer customers the benefits of seamless global communications services," MCI Chairman Bert Roberts said. "Portugal Telecom is an ideal strategic partner for MCI and BT as we bring the benefits of competition to customers around the world."
MCI said the pact let Portugal Telecom leverage BT's and MCI's capabilities to support its strategy of expanding in the increasingly competitive European market.
Portugal Telecom would work with MCI and BT to develop its global communications portfolio, enhance its domestic service portfolio and expand into international markets and services.
MCI, which announced plans to merge with BT in November to form a new company called Concert, has also been widely tipped as a likely U.S. partner for Spain's Telefonica.
